name: First payment date for WooCommerce Subscriptions
author: Javier Carazo

sections.description:
WooCommerce Subscriptions lets you delay the first payment with a free trial, but a trial is a period, not a date: you can offer “1 month free”, but you cannot say “everybody pays for the first time on September 1st”. This plugin adds that date to every subscription product and variation, and works out the trial for each customer on the day they buy.

✅ Tested with WordPress 7.2 and WooCommerce 11

✅ HPOS compatible

✅ Free, no account and no settings page: just one field in the product

📅 What you can do

  • Fixed date: every customer pays for the first time on the same day, for example the day your course or season starts
  • Calculated date: first day of next month or first day of next year, so the date moves on its own and you never have to edit the product again
  • Per variation: each variation of a variable subscription has its own first payment date
  • Bulk edit: set the same fixed date in all the variations at once from “Bulk actions”
  • Payment preview: below the fields, the next payments with the saved settings, and a warning if a fixed date has already passed
  • Sign-up fees keep working: the sign-up fee is charged at checkout and the recurring price on the first payment date

🛒 What your customers see

  • The product page shows “First payment: September 1, 2026” instead of “with a 23-day free trial”
  • The cart and the checkout show the free days left until the first payment; only the sign-up fee, if there is one, is paid at checkout
  • Variable products update the date when the customer picks a variation
  • The products list in your dashboard shows the first payment date of each subscription

🧠 Works the way you expect

  • Dates are calculated with the time zone of your site, not UTC
  • If the chosen day does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used
  • Once the first payment date has passed, the plugin steps aside and WooCommerce Subscriptions works as usual, so nobody is charged twice
  • Compatible with the synchronisation of renewals of WooCommerce Subscriptions

⭐ Need more control? Payment Schedule for WooCommerce Subscriptions

Payment Schedule for WooCommerce Subscriptions is the premium version of this plugin. It works on top of it, so the first payment dates you already set stay as they are, and adds:

  • End date: choose when the subscription ends, with a fixed date or a calculated one (last day of next month, last day of this year, last day of next year…)
  • Many more calculated dates: any day of this month or of next month, last day of next month, last day of this year or of next year
  • Custom payment schedule: set the payment dates one by one, as fixed dates for everybody or as a number of days after each purchase
  • Payment schedule table: see how many payments will be made, when and how much, and show it to your customers on the product page, in the cart, at checkout and in My account, or anywhere with the [payment-schedule] shortcode
  • Late purchases under control: when someone buys after the schedule has started or after the last date, charge only the dates still ahead, fall back to the default billing schedule with an email and a note on the subscription, or do not allow the purchase
  • Keep the billing schedule: calculate the next payment from the scheduled date, not from the moment the last payment was processed
  • Custom messages: replace the texts of WooCommerce Subscriptions with your own words
  • Prorate the first payment into the sign-up fee
  • Premium support

sections.installation:
1. Make sure WooCommerce and WooCommerce Subscriptions are active
  2. Install First payment date for WooCommerce Subscriptions from Plugins → Add New, or upload the ZIP file, and activate it
  3. Edit a simple subscription product. In Product data → General, choose the First payment date type: a fixed date or a calculated day
  4. For a variable subscription, open each variation and fill in its first payment date, or use “Set fixed first payment date” in the bulk actions of the variations
  5. Save the product. The product page now shows the first payment date

If the fields do not appear in a new product, save it first as a simple or variable subscription and reload the page.
sections.faq:
How is this different from a free trial?

A free trial is the same length for everybody, so the first payment falls on a different day for each customer. With this plugin you choose the day, and the plugin calculates the trial of each customer when they buy: someone who buys on August 10 and someone who buys on August 25 both pay for the first time on September 1.

What happens when the first payment date has already passed?

The plugin stops changing the subscription and WooCommerce Subscriptions charges the customer at checkout, as it would without the plugin. Use a calculated date (first day of next month or next year) if you do not want to update the product.

Is the sign-up fee charged at checkout?

Yes. WooCommerce Subscriptions charges the sign-up fee at checkout and the recurring price from the first payment date on.

Can I also choose when the subscription ends?

Not in this plugin. The end date, the payment schedule table and many more calculated dates are part of Payment Schedule for WooCommerce Subscriptions, the premium version.

Does it need WooCommerce Subscriptions?

Yes. Without WooCommerce Subscriptions the plugin stays inactive and shows a notice in the dashboard.

Field does not appear

Please, save your product subscription first. By default when you create a new product, this is created as simple product and this is not shown. When you save it and page reload, it will appear.

Product variations

You can set a first date of payment for each variation. Anyway, when a user visit your variable subscription product, he will see the first payment date of the first variation (in this way works WooCommerce Subscritpions with trial periods).

How can I report security bugs?

You can report security bugs through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure Program. The Patchstack team help validate, triage and handle any security vulnerabilities. Report a security vulnerability.

0.9 – 2026-11-26

  • New: warning when the fixed first payment date of a subscription has passed, because customers who buy it now pay on the day. It is shown next to the date in the product, in the products list and in a notice of the Products screen that can be dismissed
  • New: below the first payment date fields, the next payments with the saved settings (for example “6 payments: January 11, February 11… and the last one on June 11”), to check the product at a glance
  • The information about Payment Schedule for WooCommerce Subscriptions, the premium version, is now shown where each feature would be used (end date, more calculated dates, payment schedule, prorated first payment, late purchases) instead of a long paragraph in every product. Nothing is shown when the premium version is active
  • The Premium Version link goes to the new page of Payment Schedule for WooCommerce Subscriptions, with 20% off the first year for the users of this plugin
  • Updated Spanish translation
  • Tested with WordPress 7.2 and WooCommerce 11.3.1

0.8

  • Fixed a double charge when the store used the WooCommerce Subscriptions synchronisation grace period and the first payment date had already passed

  • The trial length is no longer saved into the product when a customer adds it to the cart, it is only applied to the cart item
  • Trial lengths saved into products by previous versions are cleaned up on update
  • The plugin code is now split into namespaced classes under includes/

  • Fixed the first payment date being one day late when the purchase was made before noon
  • Fixed calculated dates falling on the next month when the chosen day does not exist in the target month, now the last day of the month is used
  • Fixed the calculated date skipping a whole month when the purchase was made on the 31st
  • Fixed a fatal error when the first payment date type had an unexpected value
